_comment: Illustrative worked example for the SKILL.md docs, filled out AS IF a new rules_enabled flag were being proposed, modeled on the shape of the real dev_scope_exemption/unmaintained_package flags (see policies/policy.rego + src/caliper/core/opa_input.py). This is a demonstration file for the hypothesis_gate.py script, not a record of an actual historical caliper experiment.
author: jdoe
claim: Warning (not denying) when a manifest's lockfile is >180 days older than the manifest file itself catches supply-chain drift that package_age alone misses, without materially increasing false-positive noise on caliper's own dogfood run.
mechanism: A lockfile that predates its manifest by a large margin means dependency resolution was never re-run after the manifest changed -- the installed set silently diverges from what the manifest declares, which is a supply-chain risk signal independent of any single package's age.

observations_explained.observation: caliper's own uv.lock is well within 180 days of pyproject.toml (repo is actively maintained) -- rule should NOT fire on caliper's own dogfood run under normal conditions.
observations_explained.explanation: Confirmed: 0 findings on a clean checkout, matches the mechanism (actively maintained manifests keep lockfiles current).

observations_explained.observation: Checking out a commit from before the last `uv sync` (stale lockfile relative to a later manifest edit in the same branch) should NOT fire the new rule if the manifest and lockfile were bumped in the SAME commit -- the mechanism is about drift, not raw file age.
observations_explained.explanation: Confirmed: rule reads the last commit that touched each file independently and only fires when they diverge by >180 days; a same-commit bump keeps the delta at 0 regardless of the commit's own age, so this case correctly produced 0 findings.
